# cloud-driver-platforms-mobile

A native iOS (iPhone) client for `cloud-driver`'s REST API, built with Swift and SwiftUI. Sibling to `cloud-driver-platforms-desktop`, but a **separate, independent codebase** rather than a Kotlin Multiplatform port of it - see "Why native Swift instead of Kotlin Multiplatform" below for why that's a deliberate choice, not a shortcut.

## Build tooling: Xcode project generated by XcodeGen, not hand-maintained

This module is **not** a Maven module (like `cloud-driver-platforms-rest`/every server-side module) and **not** a Gradle build (like `cloud-driver-platforms-desktop`) - it's a plain Xcode project, built/run with Xcode itself. Building or running it requires **full Xcode** (not just the Command Line Tools) with an iOS SDK, since it targets iOS.

`CloudDriverMobile.xcodeproj` is **generated** from `project.yml` via [XcodeGen](https://github.com/yonaskolb/XcodeGen) (`brew install xcodegen`), not hand-maintained - the same reasoning this repo already applies to `cloud-driver-bootstrap`'s shaded jar or `cloud-driver-platforms-desktop`'s Gradle wrapper: a generated artifact is more reliable than one hand-edited over time, and a `.pbxproj` specifically is notoriously easy to corrupt by hand. The generated project is committed (so it opens immediately without requiring XcodeGen), but **must be regenerated after adding, removing, or renaming any file** under `CloudDriverMobile/`, or after changing `project.yml`'s own `packages:`/`dependencies:` - run `xcodegen generate` from this directory. `xcuserdata`/`DerivedData` are gitignored as usual.

**One Swift Package Manager dependency**: [ZIPFoundation](https://github.com/weichsel/ZIPFoundation) (`0.9.20`, MIT-licensed, pure Swift, no dependencies of its own) - declared in `project.yml`'s `packages:`/the target's `dependencies:`, backing folder upload/archive extraction (see "Scope" below). Foundation has no built-in ZIP archive read/write API (unlike the JVM's `java.util.zip`, which `cloud-driver-platforms-desktop` uses for the same feature), so this was the one case in this module where a third-party dependency was the pragmatic choice over hand-rolling ZIP format handling. `xcodebuild -resolvePackageDependencies` (or a normal build) fetches it into Xcode's own SPM cache the first time - no separate install step beyond that.

```bash
# One-time (or after adding/removing a source file):
brew install xcodegen   # if not already installed
cd cloud-driver-platforms/cloud-driver-platforms-mobile
xcodegen generate

# Then open and run from Xcode:
open CloudDriverMobile.xcodeproj
```

Deployment target: iOS 17.0. `TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY` is set to iPhone only (`"1"`) - this is deliberately an iPhone app, not a universal iPhone/iPad build. Bundle id `de.lino.cloud.platform.mobile`.

## Why native Swift instead of Kotlin Multiplatform

`cloud-driver-platforms-desktop` is Kotlin Multiplatform/Compose Desktop, and Compose Multiplatform does support an iOS target. That path was considered and deliberately not taken here, for two reasons:

1. **`cloud-driver-platforms-rest` (the desktop app's networking/session layer) is plain JVM Java** - `java.net.http.HttpClient` for networking, `ProcessBuilder` shell-outs (`security`/`secret-tool`/a DPAPI helper) for keychain access. Kotlin/Native (what an iOS Compose Multiplatform target actually compiles to) cannot run JVM bytecode at all, so none of that code is reachable from iOS without a full rewrite onto Ktor/kotlinx.serialization/Kotlin-Native Keychain interop.
2. **Mobile UX needs different screens anyway** - bottom navigation instead of a sidebar, no drag-and-drop-from-Finder, no right-click context menus, touch-sized targets. The "shared UI" benefit Compose Multiplatform would otherwise offer is much smaller than it looks, since most of the desktop app's screens would need to be redesigned for touch regardless.

A hand-written Swift client against the same plain REST + WebSocket API is comparatively cheap, and gets native platform integration (Keychain, the share sheet, background transfers, push notifications) that Compose Multiplatform on iOS would otherwise fight against. The cost, accepted deliberately: **zero code sharing** with `cloud-driver-platforms-desktop`/`cloud-driver-platforms-rest` - this is a second client codebase to maintain, in a different language.

## 1. Project structure

```
CloudDriverMobile/
  CloudDriverMobileApp.swift     - @main entry point; restores a persisted session on launch
  RootView.swift                 - switches between the auth flow and the signed-in TabView
  Theme.swift                    - the visual design system - see "Design" below
  ByteFormat.swift                - plain numeric byte-count formatting (never spells out "Zero")
  FileIcons.swift                 - content-type -> SF Symbol mapping, shared by every file listing
  ArchiveSupport.swift            - isZipArchive/archiveBaseName/uniqueFolderName, backing folder upload + archive extraction
  Networking/
    APIClient.swift              - actor wrapping URLSession; one method per REST endpoint used
    Dtos.swift                   - Codable structs mirrored 1:1 against the server's JSON shapes
    KeychainTokenStore.swift     - persists the access+refresh token pair in the iOS Keychain
    SessionManager.swift         - ties APIClient's in-memory tokens to KeychainTokenStore
  ViewModels/
    AppViewModel.swift           - all mutable app state + every user-triggered action
  Screens/
    AuthScreens.swift            - Login/Register/ConfirmRegistration/ResetPassword
    FileBrowserView.swift        - the signed-in Home tab (list/upload/download/delete/navigate/move/share)
    TrashView.swift               - the signed-in Trash tab (restore, or permanently empty)
    SharedWithMeView.swift        - the signed-in Shared tab (what others have shared with you)
    SharedFolderBrowserView.swift - read-only browsing inside a shared folder, pushed from Shared
    DashboardView.swift          - the signed-in Dashboard tab (account info, storage, reset password, change email, sign out)
    MoveToFolderSheet.swift       - folder-picker sheet backing "Move to..." on a file/folder row
    ShareSheet.swift              - owner-side share/revoke sheet backing "Share" on a file/folder row
    ChangeEmailSheet.swift        - two-step e-mail-change sheet, presented from Dashboard
    ActivityView.swift           - UIActivityViewController wrapper backing the "Download" action
  Assets.xcassets/                - AppIcon (a generated 1024x1024 cloud glyph) + AccentColor
```

## Design

The visual language (`Theme.swift`) is deliberately modeled on Apple's own iCloud.com web dashboard, not default iOS list/form chrome: a deep navy-to-royal-blue gradient canvas (with two soft blurred color washes, echoing the reference's own background blobs) sits behind every screen, and content is grouped into translucent "glass" **`CloudCard`** widgets - each with a colored glyph-icon + title header, mirroring the reference's Photos/Drive/Notes/Mail widget shape exactly. `CloudRow`/`CloudFieldRow` are the two row shapes used inside a card (icon+title+trailing content, and label/value respectively). The whole app is pinned to dark mode (`CloudDriverMobileApp`'s `.preferredColorScheme(.dark)`) since this design has no light-mode counterpart - it's a fixed aesthetic, not one that adapts to the system appearance.

This did mean giving up native `List`/`.swipeActions` in `FileBrowserView`/`DashboardView` (a plain `List` can't have its own per-section rounded "card" background without fighting the framework) in favor of a `ScrollView` of custom `CloudCard`s, with a per-row `Menu` (tap the "..."/ellipsis) standing in for what used to be swipe-to-delete/download. `.contextMenu`/`.refreshable` still work the same as before.

`APIClient` is an `actor` (not a class with manual locking) so every token read/write is already serialized. It talks to exactly one hardcoded deployment - `APIClient.shared`'s `baseURL`, `https://api.cloud-driver.de` - mirroring `cloud-driver-platforms-desktop`'s own hardcoded `DEFAULT_SERVER_URL` in `Main.kt`; change and rebuild to point this app elsewhere.

**Scope of this first pass - what's implemented:**
- Auth: login, two-step e-mail-verified registration, two-step password reset, session persistence across launches (Keychain) with transparent refresh-token rotation.
- Files/folders: list the current folder, upload a file (via the system document picker), **upload a folder** (via a folder-scoped document picker, zipped client-side with ZIPFoundation and uploaded as `<folder name>.zip` - the server has no folder-tree upload endpoint, mirroring `cloud-driver-platforms-desktop`'s own `FolderZipper.kt`), **scan a document with the camera** (VisionKit's `VNDocumentCameraViewController`, multi-page in one session, combined into one PDF via PDFKit and uploaded as `"<UUID>_<timestamp>.pdf"`), **extract a ZIP archive** (a file row's "..." menu gains an "Extract" entry when its content type is `application/zip` - downloads it, unzips it locally, and recreates its contents inside a *new* folder named after the archive, disambiguated as `"test"`/`"test 2"`/... if that name is already taken; mirrors `cloud-driver-platforms-desktop`'s own `extractArchive` exactly), download a file (via the system share sheet - save to Files, AirDrop, etc.), delete a file/folder (soft delete - see Trash below), create a folder, navigate into a folder via a tappable breadcrumb trail, **rename** a file or folder, and **move** a file/folder to a different folder (`MoveToFolderSheet` - a self-contained folder-picker; the server rejects a folder move that would create a cycle, surfaced as an ordinary error). A toolbar eye icon on Home blurs and disables the listing on demand (pure client-side UI state, not persisted) - a quick privacy toggle before showing the screen to someone else, independent of navigating away.
- Trash: `TrashView` lists everything soft-deleted (`GET /files/trash`/`GET /folders/trash`), each item individually restorable, plus an "Empty Trash" action that bypasses the retention window entirely (confirmed first).
- File/folder sharing - **both directions**: `SharedWithMeView` lists what other accounts have shared with this one (grantee side, read-only - a shared file downloads through the same `AppViewModel.download(_:)` an owned file uses, a shared folder pushes into `SharedFolderBrowserView` for read-only browsing); `ShareSheet` (owner side, reached via "Share" on a file/folder row in Home) grants/revokes another account's read-only access and lists current grantees.
- Dashboard account settings: **Reset Password** (reuses the same request/confirm flow the login screen's "Forgot password?" uses) and **Change Email** (`ChangeEmailSheet`, a two-step e-mail-verified flow - doesn't issue a fresh token, since a JWT's subject is the account id, never its e-mail), alongside the existing account info/storage/sign out.
- A four-tab signed-in shell (`RootView`'s `TabView`, in this order): **Home**, **Trash**, **Shared**, **Dashboard**.
- Multi-select in `FileBrowserView` ("Select items", the standard iOS Files.app/Photos.app pattern) - batch move/share/delete of several files/folders at once, alongside the existing single-item per-row actions.
- Long-press affordances via a custom, instantly-appearing dropdown (`QuickActionMenu.swift`), **not** native `.contextMenu` - Lino explicitly rejected `.contextMenu`'s delayed preview/blur and iOS-chosen menu position in favor of a menu that appears immediately, at the exact point pressed. Long-pressing a file/folder row opens that row's own actions (the same list its "..." icon's `Menu` shows); long-pressing empty space on the Home screen opens the same "+" add actions the toolbar button does. One `LongPressGesture(minimumDuration: 0.2)` + zero-distance `DragGesture` pair is attached once, to the whole screen (not once per row plus once for the background, which would race two independent recognizers over the same touch) - which action list to show is resolved from the press point against each row's own tracked on-screen frame (`.onGeometryChange`), not from which gesture happened to fire.

- Single-tap file preview (`PreviewSupport.swift`/`FilePreviewView.swift`) - tapping a file row on Home (while not multi-selecting) previews it in-app via `QLPreviewController` for text/PDF/DOCX content types (same scope as the desktop app's own preview dialog, though QuickLook itself can render more formats than that); anything else, or a file over the matching size cap, shows an "unavailable" message instead of downloading anything.

**Deliberately not implemented yet** (see `cloud-driver-platforms-desktop`'s own README/this repo's root `CLAUDE.md` for what these look like server-side - every one of these routes already exists and works, this app just doesn't call them yet): the admin panel, live push via WebSocket, thumbnails, drag-and-drop, and pagination. Extend `APIClient`/`AppViewModel`/a new `Screens/` file the same way the existing code does - the DTOs for several of these already exist server-side and are documented in the root `CLAUDE.md`.

## 2. Performance

`uploadPickedFile`/`download` (and folder upload/archive extraction, see "Scope" above) stream via the presigned direct-to-client path - `URLSession.upload(for:fromFile:)`/`download(for:)`, mirroring `cloud-driver-platforms-desktop`'s own `BodyPublishers.ofFile`/`BodyHandlers.ofFile` - so a file's bytes are never fully materialized into memory as `Data` on that path. The non-presigned (`503`) fallback path - only ever hit against an older or non-S3-configured deployment - is not streamed (a single, whole-body `Data` request/response), the one place this app still fully buffers a transfer.

**Real, byte-level progress** is reported for every upload/download/extraction, rendered as a bar pinned to the bottom of the screen (`RootView`'s `TransferProgressBar`, visible across every tab) - see `AppViewModel.transferProgress`/`APIClient`'s `ProgressForwardingDelegate`. Only the presigned path reports genuinely incremental progress (via `URLSessionTaskDelegate`'s own byte-count callbacks); the fallback path reports a single jump from `0` to the full size once it completes, since a whole-body request has no incremental signal of its own. **Emptying the trash also shows through this same bar, but as an indeterminate spinner** (`TransferKind.emptyTrash`) rather than a filling one, since `POST /trash/empty` is a single request/response with no byte-level signal to report at all.

The blocking parts of a transfer (reading a picked file's bytes off disk, writing a downloaded file to a temp path) are dispatched via `Task.detached` rather than run directly on the main actor, so a large file doesn't visibly stall the UI even though it isn't streamed.

## 3. Data handling

No local database, no local encryption - this app is a pure HTTP client, the same boundary `cloud-driver-platforms-rest`/`cloud-driver-platforms-desktop` already document: it never sees a database credential or KMS/HSM key, only whatever the server returns over TLS. The only thing persisted locally is the access/refresh token pair, in the iOS Keychain (`KeychainTokenStore`, `kSecClassGenericPassword`, `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlock`) - never in `UserDefaults`/a plain file. Downloaded file content is written to `FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory` only long enough to hand off to the system share sheet; nothing else is cached to disk.

## 4. Safety & security

- The access token travels as `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`, never in a URL/query string.
- A `401` on an authenticated request triggers exactly one transparent refresh-and-retry (`APIClient.execute`) before surfacing an error - mirrors the contract `cloud-driver-platforms-rest`'s Java `ApiClient` and the server's refresh-token design (root `CLAUDE.md`, "Refresh tokens") both already document.
- Session restore (`SessionManager.tryRestoreSession`) confirms a persisted token is still actually valid (`GET /auth/me`) before trusting it, clearing the Keychain entry on any failure rather than leaving a dead token around.

## 5. Scalability

Not evaluated at any real scale - the file/folder listing calls (`GET /files`/`GET /folders`) are the same unpaginated, single-folder-scoped calls `cloud-driver-platforms-desktop` also started from, before that app later added `?limit=`/`?cursor=` pagination (see the root `CLAUDE.md`'s "Folder view pagination" note). This app doesn't use that pagination yet - see "Deliberately not implemented yet" above.

## 6. API surface (no public library API - key screens/view-model responsibilities instead)

This is an app, not a library - there is nothing else in this repo that depends on it. `AppViewModel` is the one class every screen reads from and calls into; extending this app almost always means adding a new `@Published` property + action method there, and a new `case` on `AppScreen` if it needs its own screen.

## 7. Notable design decisions worth knowing before extending this module

- **`APIClient` is an `actor`**, not a `@MainActor` class - it does no UI work, only network I/O and in-memory token state, so actor isolation (rather than main-thread isolation) is the right default; `AppViewModel` (which *is* `@MainActor`) is the only caller.
- **No `SwiftData`/`CoreData`/any local persistence beyond the Keychain** - every screen's state is refetched from the server on demand (`refreshCurrentFolder`, pull-to-refresh). Simpler, and correct for a first pass; a future offline-cache pass would need real thought about staleness, matching the caution this repo's server-side `EntityDatabaseClient` documents about its own cross-process staleness.
- **`AppIcon.appiconset/icon-1024.png`** is a generated (not hand-drawn), full-bleed opaque 1024×1024 PNG - a white cloud glyph on a blue gradient, matching `Theme.swift`'s own accent color and echoing `cloud-driver-platforms-desktop`'s app icon without reusing its file directly (that one has transparent rounded corners baked in, which iOS app icons must not have - iOS applies its own corner mask, and an icon with an alpha channel is rejected by App Store validation). Regenerate by re-running the icon-drawing script inline in this module's own history, or replace `icon-1024.png` with real artwork directly - no `xcodegen generate` needed for an in-place image swap, only for adding/removing/renaming a `.swift` file (`Assets.xcassets` is referenced as one folder in the project, not enumerated file-by-file).
- **Deployment target and Swift language mode were chosen for compatibility, not to chase the newest APIs**: `SWIFT_VERSION: "5.0"` (not Swift 6 strict-concurrency mode) and `ContentUnavailableView`/`NavigationStack`/`.fileImporter` all require iOS 17+/Swift 5-mode-compatible APIs only - deliberately not using the newer `@Observable` macro (iOS 17+, but with sharper edges around `@StateObject`-equivalent ownership) in favor of the more broadly-understood `ObservableObject`/`@Published`.
